Review this change for security vulnerabilities.

Changed files (you may Read these and any other file in the repo):
  - .github/dependabot.yml
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml
  - Apps/Tuist.swift
  - mise.toml

Unified diff (only + lines are new):

=== DIFF: .github/dependabot.yml ===
@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+version: 2
+
+# Tools pinned in mise.toml are NOT covered here — Dependabot has no mise
+# ecosystem. They stay a manual bump (see AGENTS.md), and `mise outdated` will
+# not surface them either, because exact pins always match their own request.
+# Use `./bin/mise latest <tool>`.
+updates:
+  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
+    directory: "/"
+    schedule:
+      interval: weekly
+      day: monday
+    commit-message:
+      # cliff.toml skips `chore(deps)`, keeping bumps out of the changelog.
+      prefix: chore(deps)
+    groups:
+      actions:
+        patterns: ["*"]
+
+  - package-ecosystem: swift
+    directory: "/"
+    schedule:
+      interval: weekly
+      day: monday
+    commit-message:
+      prefix: chore(deps)
+    groups:
+      swift-openapi:
+        patterns: ["swift-openapi-*"]


=== DIFF: .github/workflows/ci.yml ===
@@ -71,3 +71,35 @@ jobs:
       - name: Test
         # Build tests separately to avoid hangs from concurrent build + test execution
         run: swift test --skip-build --parallel 2>&1 | xcsift
+
+  # `swift build` never reaches Apps/ReachySpike — it is an Xcode target, not an SPM
+  # one, so nothing but SwiftLint ever looked at it. This job is the only thing that
+  # compiles the app shell and the Tuist manifest that generates it.
+  app-build:
+    name: App Build (ReachySpike, macOS)
+    runs-on: macos-15
+    needs: lint
+    timeout-minutes: 60
+    env:
+      DEVELOPER_DIR: "/Applications/Xcode_26.2.app/Contents/Developer"
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+
+      - name: Install Swift 6.3 toolchain
+        run: |
+          curl -fLo swift-6.3.pkg "https://download.swift.org/swift-6.3-release/xcode/swift-6.3-RELEASE/swift-6.3-RELEASE-osx.pkg"
+          sudo installer -pkg swift-6.3.pkg -target /
+          TOOLCHAINS=$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw /Library/Developer/Toolchains/swift-6.3-RELEASE.xctoolchain/Info.plist)
+          echo "TOOLCHAINS=$TOOLCHAINS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+
+      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
+        with:
+          experimental: true
+          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      # `build:app` generates the project first (depends = ["project"]). No
+      # `tuist auth login`: Apps/Tuist.swift sets optionalAuthentication, so
+      # generation works without a tuist.dev session. This repo is not connected to
+      # the server project, so there is no binary cache to pull either.
+      - name: Build ReachySpike
+        run: mise run build:app

 let tuist = Tuist(
     fullHandle: "alexey1312/reachy-mini-desktop-app-swift",
-    project: .tuist()
+    project: .tuist(
+        // A set `fullHandle` otherwise makes generation require a tuist.dev session,
+        // which CI has none of — this repo is not connected to the server project.
+        generationOptions: .options(optionalAuthentication: true)
+    )
 )

@@ -46,6 +46,22 @@ run = "swift build 2>&1 | xcsift"
 description = "Build the Swift package (release)"
 run = "swift build --configuration release 2>&1 | xcsift"
 
+# `build` and `test` are SwiftPM only — Apps/ReachySpike is an Xcode target and
+# nothing else compiles it. Signing is off: the runner has no team, and the
+# personal one lives in CLAUDE.local.md.
+[tasks."build:app"]
+description = "Build the ReachySpike app target (macOS)"
+depends = ["project"]
+run = '''
+set -o pipefail
+xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachySpike \
+  -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Debug \
+  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
+  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
+  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
+  build 2>&1 | xcsift
+'''
+
 [tasks.test]
 description = "Run all tests (parallel)"
 run = """
@@ -63,12 +79,18 @@ description = "Integration tests against a running sim daemon (start with: mise
 run = "REACHY_SIM_HOST=127.0.0.1 swift test --parallel --filter SimulatorIntegrationTests 2>&1 | xcsift"
 
 [tasks.lint]
-description = "Run SwiftLint and actionlint"
-run = """
+description = "Run SwiftLint, actionlint, and the hk version lockstep check"
+run = '''
 set -o pipefail
+PINNED="$(sed -nE 's/^hk = "([0-9.]+)".*/\1/p' mise.toml)"
+DRIFT="$(grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' hk.pkl | sort -u | grep -vFx "$PINNED" || true)"
+if [ -n "$DRIFT" ]; then
+  echo "hk.pkl references $DRIFT but mise.toml pins $PINNED — bump both together." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi

-"""

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  MISE_GITHUB_GITHUB_ATTESTATIONS: false

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: macos-15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Check formatting (Swift + Markdown)
        run: mise run format-check

      - name: Lint (SwiftLint + actionlint)
        run: mise run lint

  build-test:
    name: Build & Test (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-15
    needs: lint
    env:
      DEVELOPER_DIR: "/Applications/Xcode_26.2.app/Contents/Developer"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Swift 6.3 toolchain
        run: |
          curl -fLo swift-6.3.pkg "https://download.swift.org/swift-6.3-release/xcode/swift-6.3-RELEASE/swift-6.3-RELEASE-osx.pkg"
          sudo installer -pkg swift-6.3.pkg -target /
          TOOLCHAINS=$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw /Library/Developer/Toolchains/swift-6.3-RELEASE.xctoolchain/Info.plist)
          echo "TOOLCHAINS=$TOOLCHAINS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Cache SPM dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .build
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-swift-6.3-spm-${{ hashFiles('Package.swift', 'Package.resolved') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-swift-6.3-spm-

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Show Swift version
        run: swift --version

      - name: Build (including tests)
        run: swift build --build-tests 2>&1 | xcsift

      - name: Test
        # Build tests separately to avoid hangs from concurrent build + test execution
        run: swift test --skip-build --parallel 2>&1 | xcsift

  # `swift build` never reaches Apps/ReachySpike — it is an Xcode target, not an SPM
  # one, so nothing but SwiftLint ever looked at it. This job is the only thing that
  # compiles the app shell and the Tuist manifest that generates it.
  app-build:
    name: App Build (ReachySpike, macOS)
    runs-on: macos-15
    needs: lint
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      DEVELOPER_DIR: "/Applications/Xcode_26.2.app/Contents/Developer"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Swift 6.3 toolchain
        run: |
          curl -fLo swift-6.3.pkg "https://download.swift.org/swift-6.3-release/xcode/swift-6.3-RELEASE/swift-6.3-RELEASE-osx.pkg"
          sudo installer -pkg swift-6.3.pkg -target /
          TOOLCHAINS=$(plutil -extract CFBundleIdentifier raw /Library/Developer/Toolchains/swift-6.3-RELEASE.xctoolchain/Info.plist)
          echo "TOOLCHAINS=$TOOLCHAINS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v4
        with:
          experimental: true
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # `build:app` generates the project first (depends = ["project"]). No
      # `tuist auth login`: Apps/Tuist.swift sets optionalAuthentication, so
      # generation works without a tuist.dev session. This repo is not connected to
      # the server project, so there is no binary cache to pull either.
      - name: Build ReachySpike
        run: mise run build:app

2	# mise Configuration for ReachyMini
3	# =============================================================================
4	# Bootstrap: run ./bootstrap.sh once after cloning. No global mise needed —
5	# ./bin/mise is a self-contained bootstrap binary (mise generate bootstrap).
6	#
7	# To update the embedded mise version:
8	#   mise generate bootstrap > ./bin/mise && chmod +x ./bin/mise
9	# =============================================================================
10	
11	[settings]
12	experimental = true
13	legacy_version_file = false
14	
15	# Safety net for developers who skipped ./bootstrap.sh: wire git hooks on
16	# directory entry via the native core.hooksPath mechanism.
17	[hooks]
18	enter = """
19	git config core.hooksPath .githooks 2>/dev/null || true
20	"""
21

file.content:
# =============================================================================
# mise Configuration for ReachyMini
# =============================================================================
# Bootstrap: run ./bootstrap.sh once after cloning. No global mise needed —
# ./bin/mise is a self-contained bootstrap binary (mise generate bootstrap).
#
# To update the embedded mise version:
#   mise generate bootstrap > ./bin/mise && chmod +x ./bin/mise
# =============================================================================

[settings]
experimental = true
legacy_version_file = false

# Safety net for developers who skipped ./bootstrap.sh: wire git hooks on
# directory entry via the native core.hooksPath mechanism.
[hooks]
enter = """
git config core.hooksPath .githooks 2>/dev/null || true
"""

[tools]
# --- Swift Development ---
# Swift itself is managed by swiftly via .swift-version, not by mise.
swiftformat = "0.62.1" # Swift code formatting
swiftlint = "0.65.0"   # Swift linting
xcsift = "1.3.1"       # xcodebuild/swift output filtering
tuist = "4.203.1"      # Xcode project generation (Apps/)

# --- Documentation & Formatting ---
dprint = "0.55.2" # Markdown formatting

# --- Git & CI ---
hk = "1.54.0"         # Git hooks manager (version must match hk.pkl package URI)
actionlint = "1.7.12" # GitHub Actions linting
git-cliff = "2.13.1"  # Changelog generation

# --- Simulator ---
python = "3.12" # for sim-daemon venv: mujoco ships no wheels for newer pythons

[tasks.build]
description = "Build the Swift package (debug)"
run = "swift build 2>&1 | xcsift"

[tasks."build:release"]
description = "Build the Swift package (release)"
run = "swift build --configuration release 2>&1 | xcsift"

# `build` and `test` are SwiftPM only — Apps/ReachySpike is an Xcode target and
# nothing else compiles it. Signing is off: the runner has no team, and the
# personal one lives in CLAUDE.local.md.
[tasks."build:app"]
description = "Build the ReachySpike app target (macOS)"
depends = ["project"]
run = '''
set -o pipefail
xcodebuild -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachySpike \
  -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Debug \
  -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
  build 2>&1 | xcsift
'''

[tasks.test]
description = "Run all tests (parallel)"
run = """
set -o pipefail
swift build --build-tests 2>&1 | xcsift
swift test --skip-build --parallel 2>&1 | xcsift
"""

[tasks."test:filter"]
description = "Run tests with filter (usage: mise run test:filter ReachyKitTests)"
run = "swift test --parallel --filter {{arg(name='filter')}} 2>&1 | xcsift"

[tasks."test:sim"]
description = "Integration tests against a running sim daemon (start with: mise run sim-daemon)"
run = "REACHY_SIM_HOST=127.0.0.1 swift test --parallel --filter SimulatorIntegrationTests 2>&1 | xcsift"

[tasks.lint]
description = "Run SwiftLint, actionlint, and the hk version lockstep check"
run = '''
set -o pipefail
PINNED="$(sed -nE 's/^hk = "([0-9.]+)".*/\1/p' mise.toml)"
DRIFT="$(grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' hk.pkl | sort -u | grep -vFx "$PINNED" || true)"
if [ -n "$DRIFT" ]; then
  echo "hk.pkl references $DRIFT but mise.toml pins $PINNED — bump both together." >&2
  exit 1
fi
swiftlint lint --strict Sources Tests Apps/ReachySpike 2>&1 | xcsift
actionlint
'''

[tasks.format]
description = "Format all files (Swift + Markdown)"
run = "hk fix --all 2>&1 | grep -E '^(✔|✗|hk )' || true"

[tasks.format-check]
description = "Check all formatting (CI)"
run = """
set -o pipefail
hk check --all 2>&1 | grep -E '^(✔|✗|hk )'
"""

[tasks.setup]
description = "Show git hooks status"
run = "echo 'Git hooks:' && git config core.hooksPath && ls .githooks/"

[tasks.project]
description = "Generate Xcode project for app targets (Apps/)"
# Explicit path: /usr/local/bin/tuist (tuistenv) can shadow mise's pinned tuist
run = """
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
TUIST="$(./bin/mise where tuist)/tuist"
cd Apps && exec "$TUIST" generate --no-open
"""

[tasks.clean]
description = "Clean build artifacts"
run = "swift package clean && rm -rf .build"

[tasks.changelog]
description = "Generate CHANGELOG.md from git history"
run = "git-cliff -o CHANGELOG.md"

[tasks.update-spec]
description = "Fetch latest daemon OpenAPI spec from pollen-robotics/reachy_mini"
run = """
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pollen-robotics/reachy_mini/main/docs/source/API/openapi.json \
  -o Sources/ReachyKit/openapi.json
python3 Scripts/normalize-openapi.py Sources/ReachyKit/openapi.json
git diff --stat Sources/ReachyKit/openapi.json
"""

[tasks.sim-daemon]
description = "Run simulated Reachy Mini daemon (MuJoCo) reachable from LAN devices"
run = """
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# macOS: MuJoCo GUI requires mjpython, and uv has known MuJoCo issues — plain pip venv.
VENV=.venv-sim
REQUIREMENTS=Scripts/sim-requirements.txt
STAMP="$VENV/.requirements.sha256"
EXPECTED="$(shasum -a 256 "$REQUIREMENTS" | awk '{print $1}')"
# Explicit path: system PATH can shadow mise's python with an ancient one.
PYTHON="$(./bin/mise where python)/bin/python3"
INSTALLED="$(test -f "$STAMP" && cat "$STAMP" || true)"
if [ ! -x "$VENV/bin/mjpython" ] || [ "$INSTALLED" != "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  rm -rf "$VENV"
  "$PYTHON" -m venv "$VENV"
  "$VENV/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet --requirement "$REQUIREMENTS"
  printf '%s' "$EXPECTED" > "$STAMP"
fi
"$VENV/bin/python" -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; assert m.version("reachy-mini") == "1.9.0"'
# `gstreamer_python`'s libgstpython.dylib segfaults while GStreamer scans plugins.
# Forked (the default) that only surfaces as "External plugin loader failed" and
# the daemon then hangs before binding :8000; with GST_REGISTRY_FORK=no the
# segfault kills the daemon outright. The pipeline below needs native elements
# only, so the plugin is pure liability.
find "$VENV" -name libgstpython.dylib -exec mv {} {}.disabled ';' 2>/dev/null || true
# Without the scanner GStreamer's plugin loader silently fails, webrtcsink can't
# find the Opus encoder ("No caps found for stream audio_0") and no WebRTC
# producer is ever registered on :8443.
export GST_PLUGIN_SCANNER="$PWD/$VENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages/gstreamer_libs/libexec/gstreamer-1.0/gst-plugin-scanner"
exec "$VENV/bin/mjpython" -m reachy_mini.daemon.app.main --sim --fastapi-host 0.0.0.0 "$@"
"""

    schedule:

      swift-openapi:
        patterns: ["swift-openapi-*"]

content.text:
Looking at this diff, I've read all four changed files in full. Let me analyze systematically:

**Phase 1 — Entry points and sinks:**
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: Configuration only, no execution.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: New `app-build` job triggered by `push`/`pull_request` (safe form, not `pull_request_target`). Sinks: `sudo installer`, `mise run build:app`.
- `Apps/Tuist.swift`: Build-time config, adds `optionalAuthentication: true` — makes Tuist generation not require tuist.dev session.
- `mise.toml`: New `build:app` xcodebuild task + `lint` task drift check via shell.

**Phase 2 — Data flow:**
- The Swift toolchain download (`curl -fLo swift-6.3.pkg ... download.swift.org`) has no checksum verification, but this is a duplication of an already-existing pattern in the `build-test` job — not new attack surface introduced by this diff.
- `mise run build:app` → xcodebuild with `-skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation` and `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`: standard CI practice for headless builds; plugin/macro code from Package.swift dependencies runs regardless.
- Lint script shell: `sed`/`grep` reads trusted repo files (`mise.toml`, `hk.pkl`), captures numeric version strings, quoted variables — no injection surface.
- Tuist `optionalAuthentication`: only relaxes a UX gate, not a security control.

**Phase 2b — Parser differentials:** None — new parser logic (`sed -nE 's/^hk = "([0-9.]+)".*/\1/p'` vs `grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'`) operates on trusted repo content.

**Phase 2c — High-miss patterns:**
- CI/CD trust: workflow uses `pull_request` (not `pull_request_target`), so PR-authored code runs with restricted `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No new secrets exposure.
- SENSITIVE-TO-OBSERVABILITY: no log/telemetry additions.
- OVER-BROAD GRANT / STALE IDENTITY / CONTROL REGRESSION / SECURITY-REGISTRY FANOUT: not applicable.
- ALLOWLIST SEMANTIC ESCAPE: Dependabot `patterns: ["swift-openapi-*"]` is a grouping filter, not a security allowlist.
- UNDER-VALIDATED SINK ARG: xcodebuild args are all static literals.

**Conclusion:** The changes are all hardening/expansion following existing repo patterns:
1. Dependabot config (defensive)
2. New CI job that duplicates the toolchain-install pattern already in `build-test`
3. Tuist `optionalAuthentication` (removes UX gate, not a security boundary)
4. `build:app` mise task with standard CI xcodebuild flags
5. lint version-drift check reading trusted files

No concrete source→sink path with attacker-influenceable data and missing mitigation was found.
